I would reduce the robot’s speed so its movement is slower and easier to predict. The tradeoff is that the robot would take longer to complete the movement. ## Trial Synthesis

For all three trials, I predicted the final orientation correctly, but I did not predict the final path length accurately. My largest difference was in the arc trial, where I predicted a path length of 0.600 m, but the odometry-estimated path length was 0.457 m. One possible cause could be that the robot’s actual speed was lower than the expected speed. Measured velocity and odometry data could help determine if the robot actually traveled at the expected speed. If the robot traveled at the same speed for twice the duration, the straight-line distance would be d = vt = 0.15 * 8 = 1.20 m 

## Twice Distance

Since the robot's forward velocity is 0.15 m/s, if it drives twice as long, the time increases from 3 seconds to 6 seconds. This means it would travel 0.90 meters.
